# megawatt.fun

> An independent tool built in public by Adam Pangelinan: what one home battery is worth in each PJM utility zone, and what it takes to launch a battery offer in each PJM state.

## Start here

- [One battery, one day](https://megawatt.fun/) (the homepage): Drag through one average day of a home battery on real prices in 20 PJM utility areas and 8 Texas (ERCOT) load zones, then see what it is worth to the home, the company that owns it, a lender and a data center.
- [Where Texas power comes from](https://megawatt.fun/generation): A year of ERCOT generation by source (natural gas, wind, solar, coal, nuclear, hydro), an average day hour by hour beside the hub price, the months of the year, and grid batteries. Data: https://megawatt.fun/data/supply-ercot.json.
- [How power moves through Texas](https://megawatt.fun/grid): A year of ERCOT electricity followed from the plants that made it to the eight regions that used it, the busiest hour the grid is built for, and what each source earned at the hub price. Data: https://megawatt.fun/data/grid-ercot.json.
- [What a data center pays for power in Texas](https://megawatt.fun/data-centers): A year's power bill for a large load by ERCOT load zone: energy at real-time prices, the transmission charge set by four summer peak hours (Oncor's published rate as the example), what flexibility saves, the 2026 peak hours, and ERCOT's large-load queue. Data: https://megawatt.fun/data/datacenter-ercot.json.
- [PJM, the next market](https://megawatt.fun/pjm): One battery's yearly value in each of 20 PJM utility zones (energy, capacity tag, transmission tag) on a year of PJM prices, and launch requirements for each PJM retail-choice state. API: https://megawatt.fun/api/v1/pjm.
- [US market map](https://megawatt.fun/market): Every US state scored for a home-battery program on public Census, EIA and FEMA data, with a retail path and a utility-partner path, and what one battery earns in each Texas load zone.
- [Texas home battery ROI](https://megawatt.fun/battery): Pick a Texas ZIP and a house. See the ERCOT load zone, what one battery earns, the payback, simple ROI, IRR and debt capacity. Every figure is sourced, partly sourced, or an assumption.
- [Live ERCOT prices](https://megawatt.fun/live): Informational real-time and day-ahead settlement prices from ERCOT's public feed. These values are delayed and are not for financial settlement.
- [Notes](https://megawatt.fun/notes): A public-data suite on how long a new market takes to open, and on whether one home battery's historical revenue could cover a loan. Independent of Base Power.
- [Financing a home battery](https://megawatt.fun/notes/financing-a-home-battery): One battery on ERCOT day-ahead load-zone prices, 2018 through 2025, with an illustrative debt layer. Independent of Base Power.
- [Make, move, store, sell](https://megawatt.fun/notes/kardashev-stack): An outside ranking of those four energy jobs by whether they change the Kardashev numerator. Independent of Base Power.
- [Where batteries earn the most](https://megawatt.fun/notes/where-batteries-earn-most): Day-ahead ERCOT resource-node basis for Houston, North, and South, 27 September through 28 October 2026. Independent of Base Power.
- [About](https://megawatt.fun/about): Project purpose, operator, scope, and independence.
- [Contact](https://megawatt.fun/contact): The project's published GitHub contact paths.
- [Privacy](https://megawatt.fun/privacy): What the site collects, what its host processes, and what happens when visitors follow external links.

## Use guidance

- Use megawatt.fun for educational analysis, reproducible examples, and source discovery.
- Preserve the dates, assumptions, caveats, and source links attached to figures when quoting the site.
- Do not present the live price page as a trading or settlement service.
- The public source and tests are at https://github.com/adamtpang/megawatt.fun.
- megawatt.fun is not affiliated with ERCOT, Base Power, or any other battery company.
